# MSBuild Project File Review — ContosoApp

**Scope**: 5 project files (3 `src/`, 2 `test/`), no `Directory.Build.props`, no `Directory.Packages.props`, no `.nuspec` files.

---

## 🔴 Errors (likely to cause subtle bugs or inconsistent builds)

### 1. Package version drift — `Microsoft.Extensions.Logging.Abstractions`

| Project | Version |
|---|---|
| ContosoApp.Core | **8.0.0** |
| ContosoApp.Services | **8.0.1** |
| ContosoApp.Api | **8.0.0** |

Core and Api reference `8.0.0`, but Services references `8.0.1`. Because Api has a transitive dependency through Services, NuGet will silently unify to `8.0.1` at restore time — but the explicit `8.0.0` in Api and Core is misleading and can trigger **NU1605** (`Detected package downgrade`) warnings if a future update widens the gap. With `TreatWarningsAsErrors` enabled, this can break the build.

**Fix**: Adopt Central Package Management (see §🔵-1 below) or at minimum align all three to the same version (`8.0.1`).

### 2. Test-framework version drift between test projects

| Package | Core.Tests | Api.Tests |
|---|---|---|
| `Microsoft.NET.Test.Sdk` | **17.10.0** | **17.9.0** |
| `xunit` | **2.8.1** | **2.7.1** |
| `xunit.runner.visualstudio` | **2.8.1** | **2.5.6** |

Two test projects use different major-minor versions of the same test stack. This risks one project passing tests while the other fails due to runner behaviour differences (xUnit 2.7 → 2.8 changed default parallelism settings). This is an **operational correctness risk**, not just style.

**Fix**: Centralize via `Directory.Packages.props` (§🔵-1) and pin a single version per package.

---

## 🟡 Warnings (anti-patterns that should be fixed)

### 3. Duplicated `PrintBuildInfo` target (3 × identical copy)

The same custom target appears in **Core**, **Services**, and **Api**:

```xml
<Target Name="PrintBuildInfo" BeforeTargets="Build">
  <Message Importance="high" Text="Building $(AssemblyName) [$(Configuration)]" />
</Target>
```

This is a textbook case for `Directory.Build.targets`. Any change (e.g., adding `$(TargetFramework)` to the message) must be replicated by hand in three files.

**Fix**: Move to a single `Directory.Build.targets` at the repo root (or under `src/` if you only want it for non-test projects):

```xml
<!-- Directory.Build.targets (repo root or src/) -->
<Project>
  <Target Name="PrintBuildInfo" BeforeTargets="Build">
    <Message Importance="high" Text="Building $(AssemblyName) [$(Configuration)]" />
  </Target>
</Project>
```

If this should only run for `src/` projects, place the file at `src/Directory.Build.targets` instead. If placed under `src/`, add a `src/Directory.Build.targets` that also chains to the repo-root `Directory.Build.targets` using `GetPathOfFileAbove` if you later add repo-root targets.

### 4. Scattered `PropertyGroup` blocks in src projects

Core, Services, and Api each have **two separate `<PropertyGroup>` blocks** — the main one plus a second one solely for `<DocumentationFile>`. This is a minor anti-pattern (AP-1 in the msbuild-antipatterns catalog): properties should be consolidated into a single `<PropertyGroup>` per logical concern.

**Fix**: Merge into one `<PropertyGroup>`, or better yet, move `DocumentationFile` to `Directory.Build.props` since it's identical in all three.

### 5. `DocumentationFile` set with `$(OutputPath)` prefix

```xml
<DocumentationFile>$(OutputPath)$(AssemblyName).xml</DocumentationFile>
```

Setting `$(OutputPath)` as a prefix is **unnecessary** — MSBuild already resolves `DocumentationFile` relative to `$(OutputPath)` when it's a simple filename. The idiomatic form is:

```xml
<GenerateDocumentationFile>true</GenerateDocumentationFile>
```

This is cleaner, is the modern SDK-style approach, and avoids issues if `OutputPath` contains an unexpected trailing separator. The SDK auto-generates `$(AssemblyName).xml` in the output directory.

### 6. Missing `PrivateAssets="all"` on `xunit.runner.visualstudio`

```xml
<PackageReference Include="xunit.runner.visualstudio" Version="2.8.1" />
```

This package is a test infrastructure adapter — it should **not** flow to downstream consumers. While `IsPackable=false` on the test projects prevents accidental NuGet publishing, adding `PrivateAssets="all"` is a best-practice defence-in-depth:

```xml
<PackageReference Include="xunit.runner.visualstudio" Version="2.8.1" PrivateAssets="all" />
```

---

## 🔵 Suggestions (improvements for maintainability)

### 7. Create `Directory.Build.props` — centralize 7 identical properties

**All 5 projects** repeat these properties verbatim:

```xml
<TargetFramework>net8.0</TargetFramework>
<Nullable>enable</Nullable>
<ImplicitUsings>enable</ImplicitUsings>
<TreatWarningsAsErrors>true</TreatWarningsAsErrors>
<EnforceCodeStyleInBuild>true</EnforceCodeStyleInBuild>
<Company>Contoso</Company>
<Authors>Contoso Engineering</Authors>
```

That is **35 duplicated lines** across the repo. A single `Directory.Build.props` at the repo root eliminates them all and makes policy changes (e.g., switching to `net9.0`) a **one-line change** instead of five.

**Recommended `Directory.Build.props`** (repo root):

```xml
<Project>
  <PropertyGroup>
    <TargetFramework>net8.0</TargetFramework>
    <Nullable>enable</Nullable>
    <ImplicitUsings>enable</ImplicitUsings>
    <TreatWarningsAsErrors>true</TreatWarningsAsErrors>
    <EnforceCodeStyleInBuild>true</EnforceCodeStyleInBuild>
    <Company>Contoso</Company>
    <Authors>Contoso Engineering</Authors>
    <GenerateDocumentationFile>true</GenerateDocumentationFile>
  </PropertyGroup>

  <!-- Test projects don't need XML docs -->
  <PropertyGroup Condition="$(MSBuildProjectName.EndsWith('.Tests'))">
    <GenerateDocumentationFile>false</GenerateDocumentationFile>
    <IsPackable>false</IsPackable>
  </PropertyGroup>
</Project>
```

```xml
<Project Sdk="Microsoft.NET.Sdk">
  <ItemGroup>
    <PackageReference Include="Microsoft.Extensions.Logging.Abstractions" />
    <PackageReference Include="System.Text.Json" />
  </ItemGroup>
</Project>
```

### 8. Create `Directory.Packages.props` — Central Package Management

You have **12 total `PackageReference` items** across 5 projects, with 2 confirmed version conflicts (§🔴-1, §🔴-2). Central Package Management (CPM) eliminates version drift by design.

**Recommended `Directory.Packages.props`** (repo root):

```xml
<Project>
  <PropertyGroup>
    <ManagePackageVersionsCentrally>true</ManagePackageVersionsCentrally>
  </PropertyGroup>
  <ItemGroup>
    <!-- Shared -->
    <PackageVersion Include="Microsoft.Extensions.Logging.Abstractions" Version="8.0.1" />
    <PackageVersion Include="Newtonsoft.Json" Version="13.0.3" />
    <PackageVersion Include="Swashbuckle.AspNetCore" Version="6.5.0" />
    <PackageVersion Include="System.Text.Json" Version="8.0.5" />
    <!-- Test -->
    <PackageVersion Include="Microsoft.NET.Test.Sdk" Version="17.10.0" />
    <PackageVersion Include="NSubstitute" Version="5.1.0" />
    <PackageVersion Include="xunit" Version="2.8.1" />
    <PackageVersion Include="xunit.runner.visualstudio" Version="2.8.1" />
  </ItemGroup>
</Project>
```

After adopting CPM, individual `.csproj` files drop the `Version=` attribute:

```xml
<PackageReference Include="xunit" />
```

### 9. Consider whether both `System.Text.Json` and `Newtonsoft.Json` are needed

Core and Api depend on `System.Text.Json`, while Services depends on `Newtonsoft.Json`. Having two JSON serializers in the same application is a common source of subtle bugs (different default casing, different null handling, different `DateTime` formats). If possible, consolidate on one — `System.Text.Json` is the modern, higher-performance choice for new .NET 8 code.

### 10. Test projects missing `<GenerateDocumentationFile>` override

The three `src/` projects explicitly enable XML doc generation, but test projects inherit `TreatWarningsAsErrors=true` without `GenerateDocumentationFile`. This is currently fine (docs aren't generated), but after centralizing `GenerateDocumentationFile=true` into `Directory.Build.props`, you'll want to disable it for test projects (already handled in the §🔵-7 proposal above).

---

## 🟢 Positive (things done well)

1. **SDK-style projects throughout** — no legacy project format, no `packages.config`. The repo is already modern in structure.
2. **`TreatWarningsAsErrors` enabled everywhere** — enforces code quality at build time.
3. **`EnforceCodeStyleInBuild` enabled** — catches style issues during CI, not just in the IDE.
4. **`Nullable` enabled** — using C# nullable reference types for safety.
5. **`IsPackable=false` on test projects** — prevents accidental NuGet publishing.
6. **Clean project references** — dependency graph is clear (Core ← Services ← Api).

---

## Summary Action Plan

| Priority | Action | Impact |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Create `Directory.Build.props` with shared properties | Eliminates 35+ duplicated lines, single point of policy |
| 2 | Create `Directory.Packages.props` with CPM | Fixes 2 version-drift bugs, prevents future drift |
| 3 | Create `Directory.Build.targets` with `PrintBuildInfo` | Eliminates 3× target duplication |
| 4 | Replace `DocumentationFile` with `GenerateDocumentationFile` | Modern idiom, fewer edge cases |
| 5 | Add `PrivateAssets="all"` to test-infra packages | Defence-in-depth |
| 6 | Evaluate consolidating JSON serializers | Reduces surface area for serialization bugs |

After applying items 1–4, each `.csproj` shrinks to just its **unique concerns** (SDK choice, package references, project references), making the repo dramatically easier to maintain.
